Development uses Dockerized PostgreSQL for application records, SQLite as the local Secrets Manager substitute, and local filesystem artifact storage. Production backend and PostgreSQL services remain on premises and are not provisioned by CDK or Compose. Configuration is owned by the component that consumes it: - `frontend/.env.example` contains only the public Vite API URL, Cognito hosted domain, and Cognito app-client ID. - `backend/.env.example` contains only API, Cognito, and stack-namespace settings. Compose Watch synchronizes backend `src/` and frontend `app/` or `public/` changes into their development containers. Nest and React Router then reload automatically. Changes to package manifests, Dockerfiles, or framework configuration rebuild only the affected service. Stop the stack with `Ctrl+C`, or run `docker compose down` if it was started in the background. Compose loads the committed sanitized defaults from `backend/.env.example` and `frontend/.env.example`, then overlays the corresponding untracked localized file when present. Application records are stored in PostgreSQL's private `postgres-data` volume. The private `backend-data` volume contains only the SQLite substitutes for the system and shared Design System secrets. Generated snapshots and packages use the private `generation-artifacts` volume. Development does not read Secrets Manager or S3 and does not need AWS credentials. Cognito remains the configured authentication service. Production uses the `KolibriStackName` CDK output and reads PostgreSQL, S3, and runtime configuration through the host's AWS credential chain. To exercise the production runtime-configuration and artifact providers while retaining the development server, set `KOLIBRI_RUNTIME_MODE=production` in `backend/.env` and provide the normal production stack namespace and AWS credential chain. PostgreSQL remains the application database in both modes; production mode obtains its connection from the system secret. Infrastructure deployment configuration remains separate: copy `infrastructure/.env.example` to `infrastructure/.env` only when running CDK commands from that directory. There is intentionally no root environment template. Infrastructure bootstrap, deployment, runtime permissions, and frontend publishing instructions are in `infrastructure/README.md`.

# Kolibri review contract

Kolibri is a private, authenticated design-system compiler: an owner connects a
Figma file, the NestJS backend normalizes tokens, components and variants into a
versioned React/CSS/Storybook package, and the React Router frontend drives that
workflow behind Cognito. The `contract/` package and `conformance/` suite define
the renderer-neutral output contract. Kolibri is private and unlaunched; its
deployment workflows are manual-only and a merge is never a deployment claim.

Preserve owner scoping on every read and write, write-only runtime credentials
(secrets never leave Secrets Manager or the local substitute), explicit failures
instead of silent fallbacks, deterministic generation output, immutable contract
releases, and the documented generation-run lifecycle and event history. The
Universal Figma compatibility prompt is the authoring contract for design
systems; do not weaken it or the compiler boundary it protects.

Assess purpose and evidence rather than the number of changed files or lines.
Bug fixes, meaningful tests that raise coverage, dependency repairs and
operational maintenance serve this existing product without a new product
decision. New capabilities need repository documentation or linked acceptance
criteria that establish their need and boundaries.

Ask gaulatti for a second opinion for a product-direction or authority decision:
for example a new tenant or sharing model, a new external publication target,
a change to what credentials the backend may read back, or a new public surface.
Ordinary implementation uncertainty and repairable bugs belong to automated
investigation. Changes to review controls, coverage measurement, the immutable
contract release, or this purpose contract require explicit owner confirmation.

Every material capability and mechanism must independently score at least 80 for
fit, need and proportionality under Clouseau's shared protocol. A causal technical
finding at or above 70 blocks; unrelated features or good scores cannot average
away a defect. Integrity and review-completeness gates remain independent.

Tests must assert actual production behavior and failure outcomes. Reject
fabricated coverage, disabled tests, swallowed errors, unconditional assertions
and mocks that replace the behavior being claimed. Exactly 100% line and branch
coverage of the backend application sources under `backend/src` is the
requirement for automatic approval; the backend measures every `.ts` source
(modules, entities and DTOs included) with no exclusions. Below 100% a change
may still be reviewed, but it stays pending for a human merge. Narrowing or
widening this measurement is a review-control change that requires explicit
owner confirmation.

A passing local Clouseau review may be reused only through a signed receipt from
an enrolled trusted workstation and the matching native GitHub author. CI must
independently verify current protected policy, exact head/base and engine content,
expiry, evidence and deterministic scores. All native tests and exact coverage
remain mandatory. Clouseau owns the shared scoring, investigation, repair
bounds, evidence ledger, native approval and auto-merge; this repository owns its
purpose and real tests.

# Kolibri

Kolibri generates a React component library from a Figma design system. It reads an owned Figma file and produces CSS design tokens, typed components with Storybook stories, and an npm package that can be downloaded or published. A NestJS API runs the generation pipeline and a React web app drives it. Architecture is described in [`docs/architecture.md`](docs/architecture.md) and the generation contract in [`docs/generation-pipeline.md`](docs/generation-pipeline.md); the full documentation index follows.

> `main` do not publish images, deploy services, or update the hosted frontend.

> changed Design System, run the complete
> [`Universal Figma compatibility prompt`](docs/figma-compatibility-prompt.md).

## Kolibri local development

The root `compose.yaml` is for local development only; it is not a production deployment definition. Development uses Dockerized PostgreSQL for application records, SQLite as the local Secrets Manager substitute, and local filesystem artifact storage. Production backend and PostgreSQL services remain on premises and are not provisioned by CDK or Compose.

Configuration is owned by the component that consumes it:

- `frontend/.env.example` contains only the public Vite API URL, Cognito hosted domain, and Cognito app-client ID.
- `backend/.env.example` contains only API, Cognito, and stack-namespace settings. PostgreSQL and production generation-storage configuration belong exclusively in the stack-derived system secret.
- `infrastructure/.env.example` contains the canonical Route 53 inputs and deployment-only Google OAuth values used when invoking CDK.

There is no shared root environment file. Values that represent the same deployed resource, such as the public Cognito app-client ID, should be copied from the same CDK output into each consuming component's localized environment.

1. Copy `backend/.env.example` to `backend/.env` and `frontend/.env.example` to `frontend/.env.local`.
2. Set the same public Cognito app-client ID in the backend and frontend files, along with their other localized runtime settings. Do not add AWS, Google, Figma, database-production, or other credentials.
3. Validate and start the local stack:

```bash
docker compose config
docker compose up --build --watch
```

Local nginx exposes the frontend at `https://kolibri.dev`, the API at `https://api.kolibri.dev`, and the public health endpoint at `https://api.kolibri.dev/health`. Compose publishes ports `5188` and `3188` only as nginx upstreams. PostgreSQL migrations run before the API process, and the frontend waits for the backend health check.

Compose Watch synchronizes backend `src/` and frontend `app/` or `public/` changes into their development containers. Nest and React Router then reload automatically. Changes to package manifests, Dockerfiles, or framework configuration rebuild only the affected service. Stop the stack with `Ctrl+C`, or run `docker compose down` if it was started in the background.

Compose loads the committed sanitized defaults from `backend/.env.example` and `frontend/.env.example`, then overlays the corresponding untracked localized file when present. Application records are stored in PostgreSQL's private `postgres-data` volume. The private `backend-data` volume contains only the SQLite substitutes for the system and shared Design System secrets. Generated snapshots and packages use the private `generation-artifacts` volume. Development does not read Secrets Manager or S3 and does not need AWS credentials. Cognito remains the configured authentication service. Production uses the `KolibriStackName` CDK output and reads PostgreSQL, S3, and runtime configuration through the host's AWS credential chain.

To exercise the production runtime-configuration and artifact providers while retaining the development server, set `KOLIBRI_RUNTIME_MODE=production` in `backend/.env` and provide the normal production stack namespace and AWS credential chain. PostgreSQL remains the application database in both modes; production mode obtains its connection from the system secret.

Infrastructure deployment configuration remains separate: copy `infrastructure/.env.example` to `infrastructure/.env` only when running CDK commands from that directory. There is intentionally no root environment template.

Infrastructure bootstrap, deployment, runtime permissions, and frontend publishing instructions are in `infrastructure/README.md`.

# Kolibri review contract

Kolibri is a private, authenticated design-system compiler: an owner connects a
Figma file, the NestJS backend normalizes tokens, components and variants into a
versioned React/CSS/Storybook package, and the React Router frontend drives that
workflow behind Cognito. The `contract/` package and `conformance/` suite define
the renderer-neutral output contract. Kolibri is private and unlaunched; its
deployment workflows are manual-only and a merge is never a deployment claim.

Preserve owner scoping on every read and write, write-only runtime credentials
(secrets never leave Secrets Manager or the local substitute), explicit failures
instead of silent fallbacks, deterministic generation output, immutable contract
releases, and the documented generation-run lifecycle and event history. The
Universal Figma compatibility prompt is the authoring contract for design
systems; do not weaken it or the compiler boundary it protects.

Assess purpose and evidence rather than the number of changed files or lines.
Bug fixes, meaningful tests that raise coverage, dependency repairs and
operational maintenance serve this existing product without a new product
decision. New capabilities need repository documentation or linked acceptance
criteria that establish their need and boundaries.

Ask gaulatti for a second opinion for a product-direction or authority decision:
for example a new tenant or sharing model, a new external publication target,
a change to what credentials the backend may read back, or a new public surface.
Ordinary implementation uncertainty and repairable bugs belong to automated
investigation. Changes to review controls, coverage measurement, the immutable
contract release, or this purpose contract require explicit owner confirmation.

Every material capability and mechanism must independently score at least 80 for
fit, need and proportionality under Clouseau's shared protocol. A causal technical
finding at or above 70 blocks; unrelated features or good scores cannot average
away a defect. Integrity and review-completeness gates remain independent.

Tests must assert actual production behavior and failure outcomes. Reject
fabricated coverage, disabled tests, swallowed errors, unconditional assertions
and mocks that replace the behavior being claimed. Exactly 100% line and branch
coverage of the backend application sources under `backend/src` is the
requirement for automatic approval; the backend measures every `.ts` source
(modules, entities and DTOs included) with no exclusions. Below 100% a change

## Kolibri local development

The root `compose.yaml` is for local development only; it is not a production deployment definition. Development uses Dockerized PostgreSQL for application records, SQLite as the local Secrets Manager substitute, and local filesystem artifact storage. Production backend and PostgreSQL services remain on premises and are not provisioned by CDK or Compose.

Configuration is owned by the component that consumes it:

- `frontend/.env.example` contains only the public Vite API URL, Cognito hosted domain, and Cognito app-client ID.
